description: Test fixture (issue #355): one entry per rule shape DrugReferenceInjector.InteractionNote.namesItsPartner distinguishes, so the whole family of re-derivations of that flag is discriminated by one arrangement rather than by one case per re-derivation somebody happened to write. Every entry is a nameless unrated LONGSTUB paragraph FIRST in dataset order, then a probe row whose token/atc fields are the shape under test and which carries no severity — so DrugSafetyValidator.severityPriority ties the two and nothing but the naming key can order them, and dataset order leaves the paragraph first wherever it cannot. The paragraph is longer than MAX_INTERACTION_RENDER_CHARS, so exactly one of the two rows renders and the loser leaves the record as a withheld count: a shape that names a partner must be the row the record shows, and a shape that names none must not be. The last three entries repeat the three naming shapes with NO note, so the probe's compact and full texts are one string and comparing them cannot tell a naming row from a nameless one; a nameless shape with no note renders blank and orderedInteractionNotes drops it before an InteractionNote exists, which is why there is no noteless counterpart of those. DrugReference.Interaction.setToken and setAtc normalise nothing and JsonDrugReferenceSource adds none, so a blank field arrives at partnerLabel exactly as written here.

interactions.note: Locally curated rule LONGSTUB. This operator-authored row carries no token and no ATC code, so DrugSafetyValidator.partnerLabel returns null for it, DrugReferenceInjector.orderedInteractionNotes has no name to shorten it to, and its compact form IS its whole mechanism paragraph. Being operator-authored it is also unrated, which DrugSafetyValidator.severityPriority ranks above Major, so nothing but the naming key can order the probe row beside it.
